message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.17","text":"I also set out my purpose from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in inquiries with no way through, and everything I had disclosed to you at the outset, so that I need not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to accompany you—for I do not know how it is that I gladly desire this. Yet I first want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul happens to be mortal or is immortal; and, if it is eternal, whether it must be judged for what it has done here; whether there is, after all, anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world has come into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist. And, not to state everything category by category, I said that I wanted to learn both these things and what follows from them.” He answered this: “In brief, Clement, I will provide you with knowledge of realities; and now hear from it the matters at hand.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς ζητήσεις ἀπόρους ἐκενώθην","chosen":"I had exhausted myself in inquiries with no way through","rationale":"Preserves the image of being emptied or spent while expressing ἀπόρους as inquiries offering no path to a solution."},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο γὰρ οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως χαίρων θέλω","chosen":"for I do not know how it is that I gladly desire this","rationale":"Retains the source’s unusual expression of unexplained but glad desire rather than smoothing it into a simple statement of willingness."},{"source_quote":"εἰ οὐ λυθήσεται καὶ εἰ λυθήσεται","chosen":"whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved","rationale":"Retains both explicitly stated alternatives and does not remove the first negation as redundant."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω","chosen":"not to state everything category by category","rationale":"Κατ᾿ εἶδος indicates treating the questions individually according to their kinds."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τῶν ὄντων γνῶσιν","chosen":"knowledge of realities","rationale":"Renders the philosophical expression τὰ ὄντα as things that exist without imposing a more specialized metaphysical system."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὰ νῦν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἄκουσον","chosen":"and now hear from it the matters at hand","rationale":"Takes αὐτῆς as referring to the promised knowledge and τὰ νῦν as the matters presently relevant."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.18","text":"The counsel of God has become hidden in many ways. First come bad initiation, wicked upbringing, harsh habituation, unwholesome association, and incorrect preconception. Because of these come error, then absence of fear, unbelief, sexual immorality, love of money, vainglory, and countless other such evils. Like a mass of smoke inhabiting the world as one house, this multitude clouded the sight of the men living within and did not allow them to look up and, from the design, discern the God who created it and recognize what seems good to him. Therefore lovers of truth must cry out from deep within their breasts and call for aid with truth-loving reasoning, so that someone outside the smoke-filled house may approach and open a door, in order that the sunlight outside may be admitted into the house and the smoke inside, which is from the fire, may be expelled.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλὴ ἐν ἀδήλῳ γέγονεν","chosen":"The counsel of God has become hidden","rationale":"Preserves the state of obscurity expressed by ἐν ἀδήλῳ and the perfect force of γέγονεν."},{"source_quote":"εἰσαγωγὴ κακή, συντροφία πονηρά, συνήθεια δεινή, ὁμιλία οὐ καλή, πρόληψις οὐκ ὀρθή","chosen":"bad initiation, wicked upbringing, harsh habituation, unwholesome association, and incorrect preconception","rationale":"Distinguishes initial formation, upbringing, acquired habit, social association, and prior assumption."},{"source_quote":"ἀφοβία","chosen":"absence of fear","rationale":"Avoids the positive connotations of “fearlessness” while not adding an unstated object such as God."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ καπνοῦ πλῆθος, ὡς ἕνα οἶκον οἰκοῦντα τὸν κόσμον","chosen":"Like a mass of smoke inhabiting the world as one house","rationale":"Keeps the image of a single mass of smoke occupying the whole world as though it were one house."},{"source_quote":"ἀναβλέψαντας ἐκ τῆς διαγραφῆς τὸν δημιουργήσαντα νοῆσαι θεὸν","chosen":"to look up and, from the design, discern the God who created it","rationale":"Takes ἐκ τῆς διαγραφῆς with the act of discerning: the visible design provides the basis for recognizing its creator."},{"source_quote":"φιλαλήθει λογισμῷ","chosen":"with truth-loving reasoning","rationale":"Preserves the repeated truth-loving terminology and the cognitive force of λογισμός."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ ἐντὸς τοῦ πυρὸς ὢν ἐκβληθῆναι καπνός","chosen":"the smoke inside, which is from the fire, may be expelled","rationale":"Keeps both the smoke’s interior location and its relationship to the fire; the compact Greek permits some uncertainty about the attachment of τοῦ πυρός."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.19","text":"By the man who helps, then, I mean the true prophet, who alone can illuminate human souls, so that we may be able to see with our own eyes the road of eternal salvation. Otherwise this is impossible, as you yourself also know, since you said a little earlier that every thesis is refuted and established, and that, depending on the ability of the person defending it, the same thesis is regarded as true and false. Thus theses no longer appear as what they are but, because of those who defend them, acquire the appearance of being or not being true or false. Because of this, the whole matter of piety had need of a true prophet, so that he will tell us realities as they are and how one must believe about everything. Accordingly, one must first test the prophet by every prophetic examination and recognize him as true; from then on, one must believe him in everything and no longer examine individually each thing said by him, but receive those things as certain—apparently by faith, yet accepted on the basis of sure judgment. For through a single demonstration—the precise examination made from the beginning and from every side—all things have been grasped by sound reasoning. Therefore, before everything else, one must seek the true prophet, because without him it is impossible for human beings to have anything certain.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν μὲν οὖν βοηθὸν ἄνδρα","chosen":"By the man who helps, then","rationale":"Retains both the personal noun ἄνδρα and the assisting function expressed by βοηθόν."},{"source_quote":"ὥστ’ ἂν αὐτοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς δυνηθῆναι ἡμᾶς ἐνιδεῖν","chosen":"so that we may be able to see with our own eyes","rationale":"Αὐτοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς emphasizes direct perception with one’s very own eyes."},{"source_quote":"μικρῷ τάχιον εἰπὼν","chosen":"since you said a little earlier","rationale":"In this temporal expression τάχιον means “earlier,” and the participle refers to the person being addressed."},{"source_quote":"πᾶσα ὑπόθεσις ἀνασκευάζεται καὶ κατασκευάζεται","chosen":"every thesis is refuted and established","rationale":"Uses the paired argumentative senses of ἀνασκευάζω and κατασκευάζω and treats ὑπόθεσις as a proposition under debate."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος δύναμιν","chosen":"depending on the ability of the person defending it","rationale":"Here ἐκδικέω concerns advocating or defending a case, not taking vengeance."},{"source_quote":"φαντασίαν λαμβάνειν τοῦ εἶναι ἢ μὴ εἶναι ἀληθεῖς ἢ ψευδεῖς","chosen":"acquire the appearance of being or not being true or false","rationale":"Preserves the source’s full, somewhat awkward series of alternatives rather than reducing it to a simpler contrast."},{"source_quote":"δοκούσῃ μὲν πίστει, ληφθέντα δὲ ἀσφαλεῖ κρίσει","chosen":"apparently by faith, yet accepted on the basis of sure judgment","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between the apparent mode of acceptance and the secure prior evaluation of the prophet."},{"source_quote":"ἀποδείξει γὰρ μιᾷ τῇ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς καὶ ἀκριβεῖ ἐξετάσει τῇ πανταχόθεν τὰ ὅλα ὀρθῷ εἴληπται λογισμῷ","chosen":"For through a single demonstration—the precise examination made from the beginning and from every side—all things have been grasped by sound reasoning","rationale":"Takes the initial, exact, all-sided examination as the single demonstration on which the subsequent acceptance rests."},{"source_quote":"βέβαιόν τι προσεῖναι ἀνθρώποις","chosen":"for human beings to have anything certain","rationale":"Expresses προσεῖναι as something securely present or available to people."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.20","text":"And likewise he set my mind at rest, explaining to me who he is and how he is found, and making him truly findable for me. Through the discussion about the prophet he showed the truth to my ears more plainly than things seen before the eyes, so that, struck with amazement, I marveled at how no one perceives the things everyone seeks, though they lie before them. But after writing the discourse about the prophet at his command, he had the volume sent to you from Caesarea of Strato, saying that he had a command from you to write down and send you, year by year, the discourses and deeds of each year. Nevertheless, on that very first day, while still only making a beginning concerning the prophet of truth, he fully assured me about everything. Then he said: “From now on, observe the debates I conduct against those on the opposing side. If I come off worse, I am not afraid that you might waver over the truth handed down to you, knowing that it was I who appeared to be defeated, not the thesis handed down to us through the prophet. Yet I hope not to have come off worse even in the discourse of examination, in the judgment of those who have understanding—I mean lovers of truth—who can recognize which arguments are persuasive, skillfully fashioned, and pleasing, and which are plain and simple, relying solely on the truth conveyed through them.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς ἀνέπαυσέν με","chosen":"And likewise he set my mind at rest","rationale":"Treats the supplied ὁμῶς as an adverb of likeness and renders ἀναπαύω idiomatically while retaining its sense of relief."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ἀληθῶς εὑρετόν μοι παρασχὼν αὐτόν","chosen":"and making him truly findable for me","rationale":"Preserves the explicit claim that the prophet was made genuinely possible for Clement to find."},{"source_quote":"τῇ τοῦ προφήτου ὁμιλίᾳ","chosen":"Through the discussion about the prophet","rationale":"The surrounding references to a discourse concerning the prophet support an objective reading of the genitive, though “through the prophet’s discourse” is grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"τῶν πᾶσι ζητουμένων ἔμπροσθεν κειμένων οὐδεὶς ἐνορᾷ","chosen":"no one perceives the things everyone seeks, though they lie before them","rationale":"Renders ἐνορᾷ as penetrating perception and preserves the contrast between universal seeking and the sought things lying openly at hand."},{"source_quote":"πλὴν γράψας τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","chosen":"But after writing the discourse about the prophet at his command, he had the volume sent to you from Caesarea of Strato","rationale":"Follows the supplied nominative γράψας as sharing the subject of ἐποίησεν rather than silently adopting a conjectural first-person subject; the resulting uncertainty about the writer and commander is recorded below."},{"source_quote":"τὰς καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτὸν ὁμιλίας τε καὶ πράξεις γράφοντα διαπέμπειν σοι","chosen":"to write down and send you, year by year, the discourses and deeds of each year","rationale":"Treats γράφοντα as agreeing with the implied reflexive subject of the indirect statement and preserves both writing and sending."},{"source_quote":"ἐν μιᾷ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ","chosen":"on that very first day","rationale":"Conveys the emphasis of μιᾷ with the definite first day rather than introducing a second temporal reference."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἧττον ἀπενέγκωμαι","chosen":"I come off worse","rationale":"Renders the idiom of carrying away the lesser result in a contest or debate."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς παραδοθείσης σοι ἀληθείας διακριθήσῃ","chosen":"you might waver over the truth handed down to you","rationale":"In this context διακρίνω describes doubt or inward hesitation rather than analytical distinction."},{"source_quote":"πιθανοὶ ἔντεχνοί τε καὶ ἐπιτερπεῖς","chosen":"persuasive, skillfully fashioned, and pleasing","rationale":"Preserves the three distinct qualities attributed to rhetorically effective arguments."},{"source_quote":"λιτοὶ καὶ ἁπλοῖ, μόνῃ τῇ δι’ αὐτῶν ἀληθείᾳ πεποιθότες","chosen":"plain and simple, relying solely on the truth conveyed through them","rationale":"Keeps the arguments themselves as the grammatical subject relying on truth rather than on rhetorical ornament."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πλὴν γράψας τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","issue":"In the supplied reading, the nominative participle γράψας naturally shares the subject of ἐποίησεν, while αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος introduces a different male commander. The surrounding first-person narrative may instead suggest that Clement wrote the discourse at the other man’s command. The identities of the writer and commander cannot be determined securely from this sentence alone.","proposed_reading":"πλὴν γράψαντός μου τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
